title: Atomic Functions Addendum v2 — Wave-2 Feature Set (AF-40..AF-51)
sources: docs/SRS_DK_Bond_Tracker_addendum_v2.json (acceptance criteria for FR-27..FR-37; data model deltas)

atomic_functions.name: sole_entry_guard
atomic_functions.purpose: Enforce the D16 sole-entry boundary at the HTTP layer: the Watch List add form (AF-38) is the ONLY surface that creates positions; the monthly grid and dashboard routes reject any add-position POST with a named error, and the D15 active-position lock (AF-39) is enforced at Watch List submit before any INSERT. The grid stays payment entry + render only; no alternate add route exists anywhere in the app.
inputs: incoming HTTP POST to any add-position-like route
request origin surface (watch_list | grid | dashboard | other)
Watch List add form submission (delegated to AF-38 when origin is watch_list)
outputs: delegated handling: a Watch List add POST is passed to AF-38 (lock AF-39 runs before INSERT)
rejected add POST from any non-Watch-List surface: 4xx response carrying a named error via AF-30, no write
audit-friendly confirmation that no position row was created by a rejected request
triggers: any POST that attempts to create a position on any route
grid or dashboard template rendering (no add control is ever emitted on those surfaces)
postconditions: The Watch List add form is the sole creation path; the D15 lock (AF-39) fires at that submit before any INSERT — a blocked add writes nothing (FR-27)
Any add-position POST arriving at the monthly grid, dashboard or any other non-Watch-List route is rejected with a named error and zero DB writes (FR-27)
A rejected or blocked add never appears on the monthly grid, dashboard or watch list — nothing entered the system
The monthly grid and dashboard templates contain no add-position control and expose no add route (FR-27)
Every rejection surfaces visibly via AF-30 naming the rejected operation; no silent drop, no redirect-as-success (FR-21)

atomic_functions.name: financial_goals_manage
atomic_functions.purpose: Deliver the D17 Financial Goals surface (renamed from Home Plan): render the 'Financial Goals' tab label and page, provide CRUD for goal entries carrying target amount and target end date so multi-year (e.g. 10-year) savings plans are first-class, and compute per-goal progress. Legacy irregular savings rows (39588/10063/0) are imported as goals by the import path and appear here with values preserved.
inputs: financial_goals rows (legacy home_plan schedule rows plus new goal records)
POST goal create/update/delete form (name, target_amount, target_end_date)
accumulated savings per goal (sum of the goal's schedule rows)
outputs: Financial Goals page: tab label + heading 'Financial Goals', goal list with target amount, target end date, accumulated amount and progress
created / updated / deleted financial_goals rows
success or named-error flash per mutation
triggers: User opens the Financial Goals tab
User submits goal create, edit or delete
postconditions: The goals surface is labelled 'Financial Goals' everywhere (tab label and page heading); the string 'Home Plan' appears nowhere in the goals UI (FR-28)
Each goal row carries target_amount and target_end_date; create and edit forms accept both (FR-28)
Legacy irregular savings rows (39588/10063/0) appear as goals with values and original positions preserved — never as bond positions (FR-28)
Progress per goal = accumulated savings vs target amount, computed live from rows (no stored progress column)
Every mutation validates input before write and surfaces failures via AF-30 naming the operation; a failed mutation never reports success (FR-21)

atomic_functions.name: share_snapshot_build
atomic_functions.purpose: Build the D18 customizable offline share snapshot from the Share panel's per-section checkboxes (totals, per-bond list, monthly history, amounts visibility): generate a print-styled HTML file plus a CSV option with no server and no accounts. Extends the csv_exporter building block (AF-26/AF-27) with an HTML-snapshot variant rather than introducing a new building block. Privacy-aware: when Privacy Mode (AF-43) is active, every monetary value in both artifacts is masked.
inputs: share panel checkbox selections (include totals, include per-bond list, include monthly history, show amounts)
portfolio aggregates (AF-13), per-bond rows, monthly history rows (AF-20/AF-49)
privacy mode state (AF-43)
outputs: print-styled HTML snapshot file containing only the checked sections
CSV export of the same checked sections (RFC-4180, UTF-8, exporter conventions of AF-26/AF-27)
snapshot preview reflecting checkbox toggles without any server round-trip
triggers: User opens the Share panel
User toggles a section checkbox or the amounts-visibility checkbox
User clicks export HTML or export CSV
postconditions: Exactly the checked sections appear in the generated HTML and CSV; unchecked sections are entirely absent (FR-29)

When amounts visibility is off OR Privacy Mode (AF-43) is active, every monetary value in both artifacts renders masked ('••••' in HTML; masked equivalent in CSV) — no raw amount is present in either file (FR-29, FR-30)
Generation is fully offline: no server beyond the local app, no accounts, no network requests (FR-29)
Snapshot preview updates on checkbox toggles without a server round-trip
Every failure (unreadable data, write failure) surfaces via AF-30 naming the export operation; a partial snapshot is never presented as complete (FR-21)

atomic_functions.name: privacy_mode_toggle
atomic_functions.purpose: Implement the D19 global Privacy Mode (Zerodha Kite pattern): a header eye-icon toggle that masks EVERY monetary value as '••••' across dashboard, monthly grid, watch list, Financial Goals, share snapshot and print, while numbers, statuses and names stay visible. The toggle state is persisted in local browser storage so the preference survives reload. Lives in the route/template layer (header partial + template masking helper), not in the grid renderer.
inputs: toggle action from the header eye icon
current privacy state read from browser localStorage
monetary values rendered by any template (dashboard, grid, watch list, goals, share, print)
outputs: privacy state (on/off) applied to every page render
masked monetary values ('••••') on all money fields when on; real numbers when off
localStorage entry persisting the preference across reloads
triggers: User clicks the header eye-icon toggle
Any page render reads the persisted state before painting monetary values
preconditions: Templates for dashboard, grid, watch list, goals, share and print available
postconditions: When ON, every monetary value renders as '••••' on dashboard, monthly grid, watch list, Financial Goals, share snapshot and print (FR-30)
Company names, ISINs, statuses, dates, tenure and credit-day numbers remain visible — only money is masked (FR-30)
State persists in browser localStorage: a reload keeps Privacy Mode ON until toggled off (FR-30)
When OFF, all monetary values render as real numbers with no residual masks
Share (AF-42) and print (AF-51) inherit the mask — neither surface may leak an amount while Privacy Mode is active (FR-29, FR-30, FR-37)

atomic_functions.name: grid_auto_sort
atomic_functions.purpose: Keep monthly grid rows in the D20 order at all times: Danger first, then On-going, then Completed last. The ordering key is computed from the live D5 status (AF-14) at render and recomputed automatically whenever a status changes — a position reaching Completed sinks to the bottom with no user sort action.
inputs: grid row set (bonds with live D5 statuses from AF-14)
status-change events (AF-15 recompute results)
outputs: grid rows ordered Danger -> On-going -> Completed
re-sorted row order immediately after any status flip, with no user action
triggers: Monthly grid render
Any status change (payment edit, void, day-wise sweep flip via AF-46)
preconditions: Status engine available (AF-14) for live D5 statuses (no stored status column)
postconditions: Rendered order is exactly Danger rows, then On-going rows, then Completed rows (FR-31)

A position whose status flips (e.g. to Completed via months paid >= tenure, or to Danger via the day-wise sweep) re-sorts automatically on the next render — it sinks to the bottom or rises to the top with no user action (FR-31)
Within one status band, relative order is stable (original company-name order) — the sort never scrambles peers
Statuses are never persisted; the sort key is derived live from AF-14

atomic_functions.name: chart_data_queries
atomic_functions.purpose: Provide the query layer behind the D21 charts trio: (1) per-bond invested vs received aggregates for the grouped bars, (2) the cumulative returns series with a negative flag when the running overall balance goes below zero, and (3) the Danger/On-going/Completed status counts for the donut. Pure aggregates over the ledger and live statuses; the dashboard renders them as inline SVG with no external chart CDN — this function emits data, not markup.
inputs: bonds table (principle_tl, maturity_amount per bond)
payment_ledger rows (amount, paid flag per bond/month)
live D5 statuses per bond (AF-14)
outputs: grouped-bar series: per bond (company, invested = principle_tl, received = Till Return)
cumulative returns series: ordered (month, cumulative_received, cumulative_invested, balance) points each carrying a negative flag (balance < 0)
status counts: (Danger, On-going, Completed) integer triple
triggers: Dashboard render requests the charts row (FR-32)
preconditions: Ledger and totals queries available (AF-10, AF-13)
postconditions: Invested vs received aggregates are computed live per bond from principle_tl and paid ledger rows (zero-amount rows excluded — zero = unpaid per D5) (FR-32)

The cumulative series runs month by month over elapsed months; each point carries negative_flag = true exactly when the running balance (cumulative received minus cumulative invested) is below zero — the dashboard draws those segments red (FR-32)
Status counts are derived from live D5 statuses of the full portfolio; no status column is read or written
All three datasets are query-only (DATA-05): no chart snapshot table is stored
Query failures raise named errors via AF-30; a silent zero-filled chart is never returned on failure (FR-21)

atomic_functions.name: credit_day_sweep
atomic_functions.purpose: Upgrade status timing from month-end to day-wise (D22): a daily sweep evaluates every active position against its credit_day (day-of-month 1-28 stored per position, D26). When today's day-of-month is past the credit day and the current month's payment is still unpaid, the position flips to Danger immediately that same day. The D5 Completed logic is untouched: months paid >= tenure still forces Completed and overrides any day-wise Danger evaluation.
inputs: today's date (day-of-month used for comparison)
per-position credit_day (1-28)
per-position current-month ledger row (paid flag, amount)
live D5 status inputs: tenure, months paid (AF-14)
outputs: per-position sweep verdict: keep status | flip to Danger | stay Completed
portfolio status map after the sweep (fed to grid sort AF-44 and alert builder AF-47)
triggers: Daily scheduled sweep run
Application startup (catch-up for days the app was closed)
preconditions: credit_day present on every position (AF-50 legacy mapping or new add)
postconditions: Day-of-month comparison applied per position: if today.day > credit_day AND the current month's payment is unpaid (no row, paid flag false, or amount 0 — zero = unpaid per D5), the position's effective status is Danger for today (FR-33)
On or before the credit day (today.day <= credit_day) no day-wise Danger flip happens — the credit day itself is the due day
If the current month's payment is paid (row exists, paid flag true, amount > 0), the position keeps its computed status through month-end — no Danger flip for a paid month (FR-33)
D5 Completed logic unchanged: months paid >= tenure yields Completed which OVERRIDES the day-wise Danger evaluation — a fully tenured position never flips to Danger from the sweep (FR-33)
The flip is immediate (same day as the sweep), not at month-end; the recomputed map feeds AF-44 re-sort and AF-47 alert building
Sweep failures per bond surface via AF-30 naming the bond; a bond is never silently skipped (ERR-01, FR-21)

atomic_functions.name: notification_builder
atomic_functions.purpose: Create the in-app notification rows that back the D22/D24 alert bell: when the sweep (AF-46) or the cadence timing raises an alert condition (before-due, day-of, overdue on a position's credit day), insert one notifications row carrying position reference, alert type, channel, severity and timestamp, and expose the bell list so alert history is retained and auditable. SMS/WhatsApp/push are never built (D24 deferred).
inputs: alert conditions from the sweep/cadence evaluation (position ref, alert type: before_due | day_of | overdue, severity)
notifications table (new per SRS data model deltas)
outputs: one notifications row per alert event (position ref, alert type, channel=in_app, severity, timestamp, delivery status)
bell list payload for the header (unread count + recent items)
triggers: Sweep (AF-46) raises an alert condition on a position's credit-day cadence
User opens the header bell or the alert history list
postconditions: Each alert event inserts exactly one in-app notifications row with position reference, alert type, channel, severity and timestamp (FR-34)
Alert history is retained in-app (list + timestamps) and is never cleared by the app — the alert mechanism stays auditable (FR-34)
The bell list renders from the notifications rows; unread state is per-row, never a single global flag that erases history
Only the in-app channel is created here; email is AF-48's job; no SMS, WhatsApp or push rows/channels exist (FR-34)
Insert failures surface via AF-30 naming the alert event; an alert is never logged-and-swallowed (FR-21)

atomic_functions.name: email_sender
atomic_functions.purpose: Send the owner's alert emails personal-to-personal through Gmail SMTP with an App Password (D22/D24, one-time user setup): for each alert event on the cadence (before-due / day-of / overdue timed from the credit day), send one email and record the delivery outcome on the notification path. Credentials come from the environment (SMTP host/user/App Password) — never hardcoded. Send failures surface visibly; nothing is silently swallowed.
inputs: alert events with cadence type (before_due | day_of | overdue) and position details
Gmail SMTP connection settings from environment: SMTP host, port, sender address, Gmail App Password (from environment)
recipient (owner) address from environment or local config
outputs: sent email per alert event (subject names the position, cadence type and credit day)
delivery status recorded (sent | failed with error text) alongside the in-app notification row
visible failure surface when a send fails (named error via AF-30)
triggers: Alert event built by AF-47 on the credit-day cadence
User-triggered test-send from the alert setup screen
preconditions: Gmail SMTP App Password configured in the environment (one-time user setup)
postconditions: For each alert event on the cadence (before-due before the credit day, day-of on it, overdue after it while unpaid), exactly one email is attempted via Gmail SMTP (personal-to-personal) (FR-34)
The Gmail App Password is read from the environment only — no credential is hardcoded in code, templates or the database (FR-34, security rule)
Every send outcome is recorded (sent or failed with error text) and the alert remains visible in the in-app history regardless of email outcome (FR-34)
A failed send raises/surfaces a named error via AF-30 (or an explicit visible failure row) — failures are never silently swallowed (FR-21)
No SMS, WhatsApp or push channel is implemented or configured (D24 deferred; FR-34)
Missing SMTP environment configuration blocks sending with a named setup error naming the missing variable — it never falls back to a silent no-op

atomic_functions.name: history_window_filter
atomic_functions.purpose: Apply the D23 history window to the Monthly History table: only elapsed months up to and INCLUDING the current month are selected; future month columns are never rendered; each new month auto-appends its column from the ledger with no stored header row and no future window (unlike the legacy Excel grid).
inputs: current month (YYYY-MM, from the system clock)
earliest interest_start_month across positions
payment_ledger rows across the elapsed window
outputs: month keys from earliest start through the current month inclusive
history rows shaped for the Monthly History table (per bond x elapsed month)
current-month column flagged for highlight
triggers: Dashboard Monthly History table render (extends AF-20)
Calendar month rollover (new column appears automatically)
postconditions: The rendered column set is exactly months from the earliest start month through the current month inclusive (FR-35)
No future month column is ever rendered — a month after the current one appears nowhere in the table (FR-35)
The current month is always included and auto-appends when a new month begins: no stored header row, no manual window maintenance, the column derives from the ledger (FR-35)
The filter is a query-time window only — no header columns are stored anywhere (D3, DATA-05)
A clock/ledger failure surfaces via AF-30 naming the operation; an empty table is returned only when the data is genuinely empty (FR-21)

atomic_functions.name: date_range_tenure
atomic_functions.purpose: Validate and compute the D26 date model for Add Position and legacy import: accept exact START DATE and END DATE (no manual tenure), auto-calculate tenure months by calendar arithmetic (year*12 + month delta; day-shy nuance documented as an implementation note, not a separate rule), validate the payment credit day to day-of-month 1-28, and apply the legacy mapping (start_month -> start date, tenure -> computed end date, default credit day = start date's day).
inputs: exact start date (date picker value)
exact end date (date picker value)
payment credit day (integer, form field)
legacy row alternative: start_month (YYYY-MM) + tenure_months (for import mapping)
outputs: computed tenure_months (calendar arithmetic)
validated credit_day (1-28)
validated (start_date, end_date, tenure_months, credit_day) tuple for the bonds row
legacy-mapped tuple (start_date derived, end_date computed, credit_day defaulted) for imports
triggers: Add Position form submit (feeds AF-38 path)
Legacy import maps a workbook row (feeds AF-09 commit path)
preconditions: Workbook/legacy values available when mapping (AF-02 for import context)
postconditions: tenure_months = (end.year - start.year) * 12 + (end.month - start.month) — pure calendar month delta from the exact dates; no manual tenure field exists on the form (FR-36)

IMPLEMENTATION NOTE (day-shy): when end_date's day-of-month is earlier than start_date's day-of-month the final month is only partially covered; the shipped formula remains the plain calendar month delta (the SRS example 2025-09-03 -> 2026-12-02 yields 15 months) and this day-shy nuance is documented for implementers rather than applied as a decrement
credit_day is validated to the integer range 1-28; 0, 29, 30, 31 and non-integers are rejected with a named validation error before any write (FR-36)
end_date must be after start_date; an inverted or equal range raises a named error (FR-36)
Legacy mapping: start_month 'YYYY-MM' -> start_date on that month's default day, end_date computed by adding tenure_months, credit_day defaulted to the start date's day (FR-36)
All failures surface via AF-30 naming the failing field; nothing is coerced silently (FR-21)

atomic_functions.name: print_statement_view
atomic_functions.purpose: Render the D25 dedicated Monthly Print statement: an A4 print-optimized HTML view (the views/print slice of the csv_exporter/export surface) with exactly five sections — month header, portfolio summary, this-month payment table, status list, alerts footer. Privacy-aware: when Privacy Mode (AF-43) is active every monetary value is masked before layout.
inputs: target month (default: current month)
portfolio summary figures (AF-13)
this-month payment rows from the ledger
live D5 status list (AF-14) and alert history rows (AF-47)
privacy mode state (AF-43)
outputs: A4 print-optimized HTML page: month header, portfolio summary, this-month payment table, status list, alerts footer
masked monetary values in all sections when Privacy Mode is active
triggers: User opens the Monthly Print view / triggers browser print preview
postconditions: The view contains exactly the five sections — month header, portfolio summary, this-month payment table, status list, alerts footer — laid out to fit an A4 page (FR-37)
When Privacy Mode is active, every monetary value in summary, payment table and footer renders as '••••'; the printed sheet shows no real amount (FR-37, FR-30)
When Privacy Mode is off, real monetary values appear and statuses, names and dates are complete (FR-37)
Figures are computed live at render time (no stored snapshot); the view is privacy-aware through AF-43's masking path, not a private copy of the numbers
Render failures surface via AF-30 naming the print operation; a partially filled statement is never presented as complete (FR-21)

change_record: addendum v2.0 extends Atomic_Functions_addendum_v1 after owner decisions D16-D26 (2026-10-30); adds AF-40..AF-51 covering FR-27..FR-37 only. Element placement notes: AF-41 (financial_goals_manage) uses route_handlers, consistent with AF-31's Home Plan view slice in the building_blocks; AF-42 (share_snapshot_build) and AF-51 (print_statement_view) stay inside the csv_exporter building block (export/views surface) rather than introducing a new share module; AF-43/AF-47/AF-48 are route_handlers/template-layer (privacy is a header+template concern, not a month_grid_renderer concern). AF-01..AF-39 and all earlier coverage_map entries remain owned by their source documents and are unaltered. Day-shy tenure nuance is documented as an implementation note inside AF-50 (formula stays year*12+month delta, matching the SRS AC 15-month example). Test coverage is TC-67..TC-84 per docs/Test_Plan_addendum_v2.json (landed during self-check, parallel worker) and its wave placement per docs/Development_Order_addendum_v2.json.
